widgetTool.name: show_weather_usage_card
widgetTool.description: Shows a card on chat that sets each month's gas usage next to the heating degree days (how cold it was). Use it after get_usage_history when its months carry hdd and the caller is on chat, to show why usage rose; on voice, say the same in short sentences. Card values come only from that tool. No spoken pacing is needed. Call shape: name is always cx-show-weather-usage-card and all card fields go inside payload.

name.description: Always exactly cx-show-weather-usage-card (the card element this tool renders).

display_text.description: Optional. The short on-screen text of the reply: one short lead line, for example Usage follows the cold: Feb 2026 peaked at 181.5 therms. The website shows it instead of the long spoken text. Dollar amounts and dates are written in bold markdown (**$12.50**, **November 7, 2026**). The card never repeats this text.

months.description: One entry per month, oldest first.

hdd.description: Heating degree days for the month.

stats.description: Optional. The weather_stats of get_usage_history exactly as returned (heating degree days against last month, gas used this month, the peak month): shown as a facts row under the chart.

payload.description: The card data. Put every card field inside this object.

textResponseConfig.textResponseInstruction: Write this text as the full spoken explanation, exactly as a person would say it on a phone call: plain natural spoken sentences, built only from the tool results and nothing invented, that say every fact the card shows once (the card is never repeated afterwards). Say every amount, percentage and date in words (for example forty-one dollars and one cent, the twenty-sixth of October), never digits, dollar signs or symbols, and say a year in words too (twenty twenty-six); a confirmation or claim number is the one exception and is read as returned in short groups. Use no emoji, markdown, bullets, tables, symbols or line breaks, because the voice may read this text aloud. Say how the usage followed the cold: the month with the peak usage and its amount, then every fact of the stats row of the card (the heating degree days now against last month, the gas used this month, the peak month with its usage), using the unit. The short on-screen text goes only in display_text of the card payload (always pass it, written in the customer's language; digits and symbols are allowed there): the shape Usage follows the cold: [month] peaked at [usage] therms, with the real figures; the facts row of the card shows the rest. This text is the whole reply, so write no other text and no separate pacing sentence. When the tool call failed there is no card and the text stays short.
